questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
What is an example of market failure?

options.A: atmospheric pollution in cities due to emissions from cars
options.B: free entry for children to an art gallery
options.C: high rents for housing occupied by low income households
options.D: the inability of some football supporters to afford tickets to watch games

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s long-run cost and revenue curves. costs, revenue LRMC LRAC AR MR O A B C D output At which level of output is the firm both allocatively and productively efficient?

options.A: OA B OB C OC D OD

questions.questionText: When does the slope of a budget line always change?

options.A: A person buys more of one of the two goods.
options.B: A person’s income changes.
options.C: One of the two goods becomes more desirable.
options.D: The price of one of the two goods changes.

questions.questionText: The points in the diagram represent different combinations of good X and good Y. good X N L M K O good Y An individual prefers more of both goods to fewer, but would prefer not to give up even a single unit of X to obtain additional units of Y. How would she rank (in descending order of preference) the combinations shown in the diagram?

options.A: KLMN B LNKM C MKNL D NMLK

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s total cost curve. At which level of output will the firm’s marginal cost be equal to its average cost? TC total cost O

options.A: B C D quantity

questions.questionText: What is necessary for a firm to practise price discrimination?

options.A: There are many buyers in the market.
options.B: There are many firms in the market.
options.C: The markets can be separated.
options.D: The price elasticity of demand for the product is inelastic.

questions.questionText: A mobile (cell) telephone manufacturing company takes over an electronic chip design company. This is an example of which type of growth?

options.A: horizontal
options.B: lateral
options.C: vertical backwards
options.D: vertical forwards

questions.questionText: An imperfectly competitive firm was making supernormal profits. The following year it made normal profit with no change in output. How could this situation be shown on a diagram for an imperfectly competitive firm?

options.A: by a movement to the left of the average revenue curve
options.B: by a movement to the right of the marginal revenue curve
options.C: by a shift to the right of the marginal cost curve
options.D: by an upward shift in the average cost curve

questions.questionText: What is implied by an observation that an industry is contestable?

options.A: Barriers to entry make little difference to a firm’s monopoly power.
options.B: Firms in the industry can earn abnormal profits in the long run.
options.C: Inefficient firms can survive in the industry in the long run.
options.D: Monopoly power is not necessarily exploited.

questions.questionText: What is likely to facilitate the growth of large firms in an economy?

options.A: an industry structure which approximates to perfect competition
options.B: dividend payments are a low proportion of company profits
options.C: government regulations preventing takeovers
options.D: the existence of managerial diseconomies of scale

questions.questionText: A firm changes its objective from maximising profit to producing at the allocatively efficient output. In which market structure must the firm operate for this to cause the least change in economic welfare?

options.A: monopolistic competition
options.B: monopoly
options.C: oligopoly
options.D: perfect competition

questions.questionText: Which government policy is intended to correct ‘market failure’?

options.A: guaranteed minimum prices for farmers producing certain agricultural products
options.B: imposition of taxes on factories releasing pollutants into rivers
options.C: rent controls on housing occupied by low income individuals
options.D: the provision of free books for children of poorer households

questions.questionText: The chart shows changes in employment by sector for a country between 2010 and 2016. % change in employment tertiary primary secondary –2 –4 –6 Which statement about the period 2010 to 2016 must be correct for this country?

options.A: Employment in service industries increased.
options.B: The primary sector lost more workers than the secondary sector.
options.C: There was no change in the total working population.
options.D: Unemployment stayed constant.

questions.questionText: An engineer is paid $100000 a year. The next best paid job she could get is as a teacher at $60000 a year. What are her transfer earnings and her economic rent? transfer earnings economic rent $ $

options.A: 60000 zero
options.C: 100000 zero

questions.questionText: What will necessarily cause the supply curve of labour in a particular industry to shift to the right?

options.A: a fall in wages paid in similar occupations
options.B: a greater use of machinery
options.C: an increase in demand for the product
options.D: a strengthening of trade union influence in the industry

questions.questionText: A café owner near a beach employed five staff and paid them each $10 an hour. During the holiday season two extra staff were needed. To get extra staff the employer had to increase the hourly rate for all staff to $12 an hour. What was the marginal cost each hour of employing two extra staff?
The diagram shows an economy’s production possibility curve. output of capital Y goods X O output of consumer goods What causes a movement from point X to point Y?

options.A: a positive output gap
options.B: a recession
options.C: actual economic growth
options.D: potential economic growth

questions.questionText: In an economy real national output increases more rapidly than the increase in employment. What could account for this?

options.A: a decrease in the general price level
options.B: an improvement in the country’s terms of trade
options.C: an increase in labour productivity
options.D: an increase in the size of the labour force

questions.questionText: The table shows what has happened to three economic indicators between two years in a country. When would GDP have been the most accurate measure of the standard of living in that country? population inflation rate income distribution

options.A: constant low and stable equal
options.B: constant low and unstable unequal
options.C: rising low and stable equal
options.D: rising low and unstable unequal

questions.questionText: What is assumed in the explanation of cyclical unemployment?

options.A: Employers employ more labour if aggregate demand decreases.
options.B: Exchange rates ensure the value of imports is always equal to the value of exports.
options.C: Interest rates make planned investment equal to planned savings.
options.D: Money wages are inflexible in a downward direction.

questions.questionText: According to JM Keynes, sometimes monetary policy is ineffective. The supply of money (MS) is assumed to be controlled by the central bank. The demand for money is LP and there has been an increase in real income in the economy. In the diagram which position makes monetary policy ineffective? LP LP

The US economy, which relies heavily on international trade to obtain raw materials and to sell products, is in equilibrium at point X. If the value of the US$ falls, what would be the new equilibrium point? price level AS B

options.A: C X D AD O real GDP

questions.questionText: From any additional national income, 20% is spent on imports, 25% is paid in taxes, 5% is saved and the rest is spent on domestically produced goods. According to the multiplier effect, if exports increase by $100 million, what will be the final increase in spending by the country’s residents on domestically produced goods?

options.A: $50 million B $100 million C $200 million D $500 million

questions.questionText: In a Keynesian model, why would a $100 million increase in government expenditure on goods and services have a greater impact on aggregate demand than a $100 million reduction in tax revenue?

options.A: Consumers spend only part of any extra disposable income.
options.B: Government expenditure does not create wealth.
options.C: The marginal tax rate affects the value of the multiplier.
options.D: The multiplier does not apply to consumer expenditure.

questions.questionText: Equilibrium income in the economy is the level of national income at which

options.A: the economy is producing at full employment national income.
options.B: the inflow and outflow of currency is equal.
options.C: the government’s expenditure is equal to the government’s revenue.
options.D: there is no tendency for the national income to change.

questions.questionText: What is not an automatic stabiliser?

options.A: income tax
options.B: profits tax
options.C: state retirement pension
options.D: unemployment benefit

questions.questionText: Which policy is most likely to allow a developed economy to meet all its macroeconomic objectives?

options.A: lowering interest rates to raise actual growth above potential growth
options.B: supply-side reform to increase product and factor market flexibility
options.C: tax reform to make the system of taxation increasingly regressive
options.D: the introduction of tariffs to protect domestic industry

questions.questionText: A government is increasing the role of market forces in its economy. However, it imposed temporary maximum price controls. Why might a government, committed to reducing central planning, introduce price controls?

options.A: to increase allocative efficiency
options.B: to increase the incentive for producers to raise supply
options.C: to reduce consumer demand
